archived	openspec/changes/archive/2026-04-18-add-performance-review-kit/design.md	7	A compile-time lint pass is the wrong first move here. Static detection would either miss the important cases or over-warn on code that is structurally similar but operationally harmless.

archived	openspec/changes/archive/2026-04-18-add-performance-review-kit/design.md	29	**Rationale:** Tiger Style performance rules are strongest during design and review: napkin math, batching, control-plane/data-plane separation, and cost × frequency ranking all depend on workload intent. Any consumer-integration helper that launches the CLI from a temp consumer workspace must keep the cwd at that temp workspace and invoke the binary via an explicit `--manifest-path /path/to/tigerstyle/cargo-tigerstyle/Cargo.toml` (or the already-built binary path) instead of `cargo run -p cargo-tigerstyle` from the temp workspace.

archived	openspec/changes/archive/2026-04-24-structured-check-output/design.md	38	**Lint name filtering:** Dylint-based lints currently emit bare lint names in the `message.code.code` field (e.g., `no_unwrap`, not `tigerstyle::no_unwrap`). The filter accepts any `code.code` value that matches a `lint_name` entry in `DIAGNOSTIC_METADATA`. If tool-scoped names are added in the future, the filter also accepts `code.code` values starting with `tigerstyle::` and strips the prefix for lookup. This handles the mixed bare/tool-scoped state documented in the napkin without requiring changes to the lint library.

archived	openspec/changes/archive/2026-04-24-structured-check-output/proposal.md	12	**Parsing strategy:** `cargo tigerstyle check` will pass `--message-format=json` to the underlying `cargo check` invocation and parse rustc's JSON diagnostic objects from the child process stdout. This is the same mechanism used by `cargo clippy --message-format=json` and `rust-analyzer`. Dylint-based lints flow through rustc's standard diagnostic pipeline, so their JSON output includes lint name, spans, suggestions, and applicability — all fields needed for structured output.
